result.title: PI-MLLM: Psychophysics-Inspired Multimodal Large Language Model for Oddly Satisfying Video Emotion Analysis
result.comment: 12 pages, 5 figures, 8 tables; includes supplementary material
result.summary: Oddly Satisfying Videos (OSVs) can evoke strong viewer responses through repetitive motion, visual tactility, and ASMR-like sounds despite containing few explicit semantic emotion cues. This makes OSVs a challenging setting for Video Emotion Analysis (VEA), since most existing methods focus on semantic video content and under-model the physical sensory dynamics that shape viewer responses. To support Oddly Satisfying Video Emotion Analysis (OSVEA), we construct the Oddly Satisfying Video Dataset (OSVD), comprising 12,000 annotated 5-second clips. Each clip provides viewer-emotion labels under video-only, audio-only, and audio-visual conditions, together with explanations grounded in visual and acoustic sensory evidence. Building on OSVD, we propose PI-MLLM, a psychophysics-inspired multimodal large language model that integrates Modality-Specific Dynamics Alignment (MSDA) and Coalition-Based Audio-Visual Attribution (CAVA). MSDA uses auxiliary prediction objectives to align modality representations with visual motion and acoustic energy-onset dynamics. CAVA evaluates emotion scores across modality coalitions and applies Shapley attribution to identify the dominant modality and determine whether visual and auditory evidence is synergistic or conflicting. Experiments show that PI-MLLM improves both viewer-side emotion prediction and sensory-grounded explanation quality, suggesting the value of physical sensory cues to video emotion analysis.

AI.brief_summary: 构建含 12,000 个 5 秒片段的 OSVD 数据集，提供单模态与音视频条件下的情绪标签及感官依据解释，并提出心理物理学启发的 MLLM：用辅助预测目标对齐模态表示与视觉运动、声音能量起始动态，再用基于模态联盟的 Shapley 归因判断主导模态及视听证据是协同还是冲突。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文主线是视频情绪分析而非 latent 推理，但其按模态联盟做 Shapley 贡献归因、区分协同与冲突证据的做法，可供核查能否迁移到 LVR 中视觉证据是否被使用、模态旁路贡献分配的诊断上。
